Hi Sandeep,

Quick touch to confirm we’re aligned on timelines for your November 1 renewal. I reviewed usage and support history with my team — there were two production incidents in Q3 that drove some unexpected load and latencies; I appreciate the patience from your engineers.

You mentioned wanting to explore a concession to address the recent reliability impact and the headcount reshuffle at Elm Street that reduced short-term usage. If you can send a short list of what you’re looking for (credit amount, term preference, SLA add-on), I’ll route it via our deal desk and get an exec decision window.

CCing Karthik (pricing) and Marissa (region lead) so we can move quickly. Would you be open to a 30-min call tomorrow if needed?

Thanks,

From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@elmstreet.ai>

Date: 2026-10-16T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elm Street upcoming renewal — touchpoint

Alex —

Thanks for reaching out. We want to be candid: the Q3 incidents hit our production SLAs and we reallocated spend elsewhere while our infra team stabilized things. We still value Redwood’s latency profile overall but need a commercial reset to move forward. Our ask is: 1) a one-time operational credit to offset the incidents (~$75k), 2) a one-year term reset so we can align usage expectations, and 3) a written SLA addendum that guarantees a remediation credit if p99 latency/availability thresholds are missed.

If Redwood can give us those three items we’ll sign an updated SOW and commit to a renewed contract. I attached a short incident summary and our purchasing team’s contract contact.

-Sandeep
VP Engineering, Elm Street AI
sandeep@elmstreet.ai

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-17T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Elm Street renewal concession request — need exec review

Team — forwarding Elm Street’s asks and incident summary. Quick context: Elm Street is a mid-market AI infra customer, current ARR ~$420k, renewal due 2026-11-01. They’re requesting:

- $75k one-time operational credit for Q3 incident impact
- One-year term reset (move renewal date + reset committed spend)
- Formal SLA addendum with remediation credits for p99/availability misses

Impact/ask: if we grant as requested, near-term revenue will drop vs. current ARR because the credit + term reset will reduce recognized near-term ARR; however, they’ve indicated willingness to sign if we accept. My recommendation is to offer a counter: 20% discount on first renewal invoice + $50k one-time credit + SLA addendum, in exchange for a committed 18-month deal and a 10% uplift to committed units.

Please find attached the usage report and Elm Street’s incident bundle. Need clear guidance: approve full ask (75k + reset) OR approve counter (20% + 50k + SLA) OR escalate to execs for exception above $60k credit.

Thanks,
Alex

Attachments: ElmStreet_SOW_v3.pdf, elmstreet_support_ticket_Q3.zip, usage_report_Q3.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Elm Street renewal concession request — need exec review

Alex —

Quick pricing analysis attached inline. High level:
- Approving $75k credit is ~18% of annual contract value; that’s outside standard deal desk automated concessions for this cohort.
- Counter proposed (20% + $50k one-time) moves us closer to a middle ground.
- Term reset increases churn risk in Q1 but the 18-month committed uplift mitigates it if Elm Street executes.

Recommendation: Approve the counter (20% + $50k credit) via deal desk sign-off. Anything above $60k credit requires regional VP approval (Marissa) and finance acknowledgement (Naomi). For the SLA addendum, legal needs to draft a limited-scope SLA that limits remediation to service credits capped at the one-time credit amount.

—Karthik
Director, Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Elm Street renewal concession request — need exec review

Team —

I agree with Karthik’s assessment and will approve up to a $60k one-time credit plus a 25% discount on the first renewal invoice provided we secure the following:
1) Elm Street signs an 18-month SOW with a minimum committed spend equal to their current ARR (no recognition reset that reduces committed MRR), and
2) Legal delivers a tightly-scoped SLA that limits remediation to service credits and excludes consequential damages, and
3) Finance (Naomi) confirms the accounting treatment and cashflow impact.

If Alex can get Elm Street to accept those commercial guardrails I will sign off on the concession. Anything exceeding $60k requires direct sign-off from Vivek.

Marissa Cole
VP Sales, North America
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@elmstreet.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, contracts@elmstreet.ai
Date: 2026-10-20T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Elm Street renewal — proposed concession and next steps

Hi Sandeep —

Thanks again for the call today. We spoke internally and can move forward with a limited concession if Elm Street agrees to a slightly modified commercial framework:

What Redwood can provide now:
- One-time credit: $50,000 applied on the first renewal invoice
- 25% discount on the first renewal invoice (applies to committed units only)
- A narrowly-scoped SLA addendum with service-credit remediation only (legal to send draft)
- Requirement: Elm Street signs an 18-month SOW with committed spend at or above current ARR and agrees to the updated SOW via DocuSign

What we cannot do: full $75k operational credit or blanket term reset without VP/exec sign-off. If you need to exceed the offer above, we will need explicit exec approval from our leadership (Vivek).

If this sounds acceptable I’ll instruct legal to prepare the SOW/SLA and send via DocuSign. Goal is to have countersigned SOW by 2026-10-29 to avoid mid-November service churn.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.ai
